note: Case list for tools/chart_parity.py — the Phase B Flip A parity gate.
Each case is a URL for the headless /r/chart route: a committed bar fixture
(`fixedbars`), one chart preset, and a PARTIAL chart_settings blob describing
exactly the indicator under test. The harness base64url-encodes preset+settings
into ?indicators= and screenshots the #chart-export element on two builds.
The four live cases are the Flip A pilot. The rest are NAME-ONLY placeholders:
B3 fills in each one's settings blob when it migrates that indicator, so the
list already states the full obligation instead of quietly shrinking to what
was easy. `--include-placeholders` runs them; the default run skips them.
Tolerance is 0 everywhere and should stay 0 — see report.md's 'Reading this'.
A per-case `tolerance` must be accompanied by `toleranceReason`.
DO NOT change `defaults.fixedbars`, `w`, `h` or the preset without re-capturing
every stored baseline: they are part of what a baseline PNG means.

classic_flat._why: The 'Classic Dark' preset (= CHART_DEFAULTS) with the four MA overlays and the watermark removed, so the indicator under test is the dominant ink on the canvas and a diff is attributable to it rather than to an EMA that happens to cross it. Volume keeps its own pane because a pane-count change is itself a regression worth catching.

cases.name: bb_only
cases.why: Overlay on the price pane — the migration must land the three bands on the same pixels, in the same order, with the same fill.

cases.name: rsi_only
cases.why: Single-line separate pane — proves pane creation, height and the 30/70 guides survive the move.

cases.name: macd_only
cases.why: Three outputs in one pane, one of them a sign-coloured histogram. The B1 note in indicators.js says StockChart masks the MACD line's head back to the signal's first bar — this case is what proves that mask is still there.

cases.name: bb_rsi_macd
cases.why: All three at once: an overlay plus TWO extra panes. Catches pane-ordering and pane-height regressions that no single-indicator case can see.
